stories.headline: OpenAI Proposes Robot Taxes, Public Wealth Fund in 'Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age'

key_facts.fact: OpenAI published a 13-page policy document titled 'Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age: Ideas to Keep People First' on April 6, presented as a starting point for debate.
key_facts.excerpt: 13-page policy document titled 'Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age'... Presented as starting point for debate, not fixed prescription

key_facts.fact: The plan proposes a nationally managed public wealth fund seeded by AI companies, modeled after Alaska's Permanent Fund oil dividend, to give every American a stake in AI-driven growth.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI proposes seeding a national fund with contributions from AI companies. The fund would invest in AI firms and businesses adopting the technology, then distribute returns directly to American citizens—modeled after Alaska's Permanent Fund oil dividend structure.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI proposes taxing businesses that replace human workers with automated systems to compensate for reduced payroll tax revenue funding Social Security, Medicaid, and food assistance.
key_facts.excerpt: Tax businesses that replace human workers with automated systems to compensate for reduced payroll tax revenue that funds Social Security, Medicaid, and food assistance.

key_facts.fact: The document proposes auto-triggering safety nets: benefits like unemployment payments and wage insurance increase automatically when AI-driven job displacement hits preset thresholds, then phase out when conditions improve.
key_facts.excerpt: Benefits like unemployment payments and wage insurance would increase automatically when AI-driven job displacement hits preset thresholds, then phase out when conditions improve.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI proposes pilot programs testing 32-hour workweeks at full pay, framed as an 'efficiency dividend' from AI productivity gains.
key_facts.excerpt: Pilot programs testing 32-hour workweeks at full pay, framed as 'efficiency dividend'

key_facts.fact: Altman warns cyberattacks are 'totally possible' within one year and bioweapon creation is 'no longer theoretical,' describing them as the most immediate AI threats.
key_facts.excerpt: He stated cyberattacks and bioweapons represent the 'most immediate' AI threats, describing cyberattacks as 'totally possible' within one year and bioweapon creation as 'no longer theoretical.'

key_facts.fact: Altman told Axios that AI superintelligence is so close and disruptive that America needs a new social contract on the scale of the Progressive Era and the New Deal during the Great Depression.
key_facts.excerpt: Altman told Axios he feels such urgency about the power of coming AI models that OpenAI is unveiling a New Deal for superintelligence... He says AI will soon be so mindbending that America needs a new social contract

stories.headline: Tufts Neuro-Symbolic AI Achieves 95% Accuracy With 100x Less Energy Than Standard Models

key_facts.fact: Researchers at Tufts University led by Matthias Scheutz developed a neuro-symbolic visual-language-action (VLA) system that combines neural networks with symbolic reasoning, achieving up to 100x energy reduction.
key_facts.excerpt: Researchers have unveiled a radically more efficient approach that could slash AI energy use by up to 100x while actually improving accuracy... led by Matthias Scheutz, Karol Family Applied Technology Professor

key_facts.fact: The neuro-symbolic VLA achieved a 95% success rate on the Tower of Hanoi puzzle, compared with just 34% for standard systems, and 78% on unfamiliar complex variants where traditional models scored 0%.
key_facts.excerpt: Neuro-symbolic VLA achieved 95% success rate vs. 34% for standard systems on Tower of Hanoi puzzle. Achieved 78% success on unfamiliar complex puzzle variants (traditional models: 0%)

key_facts.fact: Training required only 1% of the energy of standard VLA systems (34 minutes vs. 36+ hours), and operational energy consumption was just 5% of conventional approaches.
key_facts.excerpt: Training requires only 1% of energy used by standard VLA systems. Operational energy consumption: 5% of conventional approaches. Training time: 34 minutes vs. 36+ hours for conventional approaches

key_facts.fact: The approach focuses on robotics VLA models that extend LLM capabilities by incorporating vision and physical movement, unlike chatbot-style LLMs like ChatGPT.
key_facts.excerpt: Unlike familiar large language models such as ChatGPT and Gemini, the team focuses on AI systems used in robotics known as visual-language-action (VLA) models, which extend LLM capabilities by incorporating vision and physical movement.

key_facts.fact: The work will be presented at the International Conference of Robotics and Automation (ICRA) in Vienna in May 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The work will be presented at the International Conference of Robotics and Automation in Vienna in May

key_facts.excerpt: The framework—drafted by Pakistan—was exchanged overnight with both Tehran and Washington, describing a phased approach beginning with an immediate ceasefire followed by a comprehensive agreement

key_facts.fact: The plan includes Iranian commitments to abandon pursuit of nuclear weapons in exchange for sanctions relief and the release of frozen assets, with Pakistan serving as the sole communication channel.
key_facts.excerpt: Pakistan shares ceasefire framework to end US-Iran war

key_facts.fact: Iran rejected the idea of reopening the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for a temporary ceasefire, with a senior official telling Reuters that Tehran views Washington as lacking readiness for a permanent ceasefire.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran won't reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for a 'temporary ceasefire'

key_facts.fact: Neither Iran nor the US had formally responded to the proposal as of Sunday night. Pakistani officials said ceasefire efforts were 'at an advanced stage' but faced 'several spoilers and detractors.'
key_facts.excerpt: Neither Iran nor the U.S. had responded to the proposal

stories.headline: Artemis II Completes Course Correction, Crew Set for Historic Lunar Flyby

key_facts.fact: The Orion spacecraft completed a 17.5-second outbound correction burn at 11:03 p.m. EDT on April 5 to refine its trajectory toward the Moon.
key_facts.excerpt: The outbound correction burn occurred at 11:03 p.m. EDT, lasting 17.5 seconds to refine Orion's trajectory toward the Moon

key_facts.fact: The crew entered the Moon's sphere of influence at 12:41 a.m. EDT on April 6. The flyby window runs from 2:45-9:40 PM EDT April 6, with closest approach at 4,070 miles from the lunar surface at 7:02 p.m.
key_facts.excerpt: The crew enters the Moon's sphere of influence at 12:41 a.m. on April 6

key_facts.fact: At 1:56 p.m. EDT April 6, the crew will surpass Apollo 13's record for humans' farthest distance from Earth, reaching a maximum distance of 252,757 miles—4,105 miles farther than Apollo 13.
key_facts.excerpt: 1:56 p.m.: Crew surpasses Apollo 13's distance record from Earth

key_facts.fact: All four crew members—Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen—completed testing of the Orion Crew Survival System suits including pressurization, leak checks, and simulated seat entry.
key_facts.excerpt: putting on and pressurizing the suit, performing leak checks, simulating seat entry, and assessing mobility and their ability to eat and drink

key_facts.fact: NASA scientists identified about 35 geological features for the crew to observe during the flyby. The crew will work in pairs to photograph sites and describe them in real time to Mission Control.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA's Artemis II crew readies for Monday's lunar flyby

key_facts.fact: Orion will pass behind the Moon at 6:44 p.m. EDT, losing communications for approximately 40 minutes. 'Earthrise' and signal reacquisition are expected at 7:25 p.m.
key_facts.excerpt: 6:44 p.m.: Loss of communications as Orion passes behind the Moon (~40 minutes)

stories.headline: Drift Reveals $270M Crypto Exploit Was a Six-Month North Korean Intelligence Op

key_facts.fact: Drift Protocol, the largest decentralized perpetual futures exchange on Solana, revealed on April 5 that its $270M exploit on April 1 was a six-month intelligence operation by a North Korean state-affiliated group.
key_facts.excerpt: Drift says $270 million exploit was a six-month North Korean intelligence operation

key_facts.fact: The attackers first made contact at a major crypto conference around fall 2025, posing as a quantitative trading firm. They onboarded an Ecosystem Vault, deposited over $1 million of their own capital, and held multiple working sessions with contributors.
key_facts.excerpt: Attackers posed as a trading firm, met Drift contributors in person across multiple countries, deposited $1 million of their own capital

key_facts.fact: The attacker abused Solana's 'durable nonces' feature to pre-sign transactions that remained valid for over a week, then obtained two misleading approvals from Drift's five-member Security Council multisig to seize protocol control in minutes.
key_facts.excerpt: Here is how Drift attackers drained more than $270 million using a Solana feature designed for convenience

key_facts.fact: Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic flagged the exploit as consistent with previous DPRK-attributed operations based on on-chain behavior, laundering methodologies, and network-level indicators. Total DPRK crypto theft in 2026 exceeds $300 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Drift Protocol exploited for $286 million in suspected DPRK-linked attack

key_facts.fact: TRM Labs confirmed the attack represents the eighteenth DPRK-linked crypto operation tracked in 2026, making North Korea the most prolific state-sponsored crypto threat actor.
key_facts.excerpt: North Korean Hackers Attack Drift Protocol In USD 285 Million Heist
